pr.title: Add invoice rebate codes
pr.body:
Fixes #1

Adds an optional invoice-level rebate code, keeps an explicit calculation argument as an override, and adds validation and focused tests. The existing discount helper is renamed mechanically as part of the cleanup.
pr.author: ToukoUrsin

requirement.title: Add invoice-level rebate codes and transparent totals
requirement.body:
The invoice engine should support a customer rebate code when calculating totals.

Acceptance criteria:
- WELCOME applies a 5% rebate to every invoice subtotal.
- PARTNER applies a 10% rebate only when the subtotal is at least EUR 1,000.
- NONPROFIT applies a 15% rebate only when the subtotal is at least EUR 500.
- Rebate and tax amounts are rounded to cents and the final total equals taxable amount plus tax.
- Existing callers that omit a code retain current totals.

Ambiguity: the requirement does not say whether the minimum threshold is evaluated before or after line-level rounding.

criteria.text: When the WELCOME code is supplied, the rebate equals 5% of the invoice subtotal for any subtotal amount, including small ones.
criteria.sourceQuote: WELCOME applies a 5% rebate to every invoice subtotal.
criteria.note: With WELCOME on small subtotals (0.10 and 3×1.10), asserts the rebate equals 5% of the subtotal rounded to the cent (0.01 and 0.17). Expected to FAIL on head too: the rebate is applied to each line and rounded per line, so a 0.10 invoice gets a 0.00 rebate.

criteria.text: When the PARTNER code is supplied, a 10% rebate is applied if the subtotal is EUR 1,000.00 or more (including exactly EUR 1,000.00), and no rebate is applied if the subtotal is below EUR 1,000.00.
criteria.sourceQuote: PARTNER applies a 10% rebate only when the subtotal is at least EUR 1,000.
criteria.note: With PARTNER, asserts a 100.00 rebate at exactly 1000.00 (one line, and also 600+400) and 0.00 at 999.99. Expected to pass on base too, because the PR changes no behaviour.

criteria.text: When the NONPROFIT code is supplied, a 15% rebate is applied if the subtotal is EUR 500.00 or more (including exactly EUR 500.00), and no rebate is applied if the subtotal is below EUR 500.00.
criteria.sourceQuote: NONPROFIT applies a 15% rebate only when the subtotal is at least EUR 500.
criteria.note: With NONPROFIT, asserts a 75.00 rebate at exactly 500.00, 120.00 at 800.00 and 0.00 at 499.99. Expected to FAIL on head and base: discounts.py explicitly skips NONPROFIT when net == 500.

criteria.text: For every code, the rebate and tax amounts returned are rounded to whole cents, and the final total exactly equals the taxable amount plus the tax amount, with no leftover sub-cent difference.
criteria.sourceQuote: Rebate and tax amounts are rounded to cents and the final total equals taxable amount plus tax.
criteria.note: For every code and for subtotals with sub-cent amounts, asserts discount, tax, taxable and total are whole cents and that total == taxable + tax exactly.

criteria.text: Calling the total calculation without a rebate code returns the same totals as before the change for the same inputs.
criteria.sourceQuote: Existing callers that omit a code retain current totals.

criteria.text: All existing invoice-engine tests still pass without changes to their expected values.
criteria.note: Runs pytest in a subprocess on the existing test_totals/test_rounding/test_formatting files and asserts exit code 0.

units.title: Add optional rebate_code field to Invoice
units.summary: Invoice gains an optional rebate_code attribute (default None), which from_lines also accepts. A blank or whitespace-only code raises ValueError.
units.readingNote: Check that adding the field after `notes` with a default keeps existing positional construction working, and that rejecting blank codes is intended.

draft.title: Add optional rebate_code field to Invoice
draft.summary: Invoice gains an optional rebate_code attribute (default None), which from_lines also accepts. A blank or whitespace-only code raises ValueError.
draft.readingNote: Check that adding the field after `notes` with a default keeps existing positional construction working, and that rejecting blank codes is intended.

facts.why: New public dataclass field Invoice.rebate_code and new rebate_code keyword on Invoice.from_lines.
__post_init__ raises ValueError("rebate code must not be blank") for whitespace-only codes.
Validation of blank rebate codes was not requested by the requirement.

units.title: Resolve rebate code from argument or invoice in calculate_totals
units.summary: calculate_totals uses the explicit discount_code argument when it is not None, and otherwise falls back to invoice.rebate_code. Rounding and total composition are unchanged.
units.readingNote: Because only None triggers the fallback, an explicit empty string "" overrides the invoice code and turns the rebate off; check whether callers expect that.

draft.title: Resolve rebate code from argument or invoice in calculate_totals
draft.summary: calculate_totals uses the explicit discount_code argument when it is not None, and otherwise falls back to invoice.rebate_code. Rounding and total composition are unchanged.
draft.readingNote: Because only None triggers the fallback, an explicit empty string "" overrides the invoice code and turns the rebate off; check whether callers expect that.

facts.why: New precedence rule: `code = discount_code if discount_code is not None else invoice.rebate_code`.
calculate_totals results now depend on Invoice.rebate_code when no argument is given.

units.title: Exclude NONPROFIT rebate at exactly the EUR 500 minimum
units.summary: discount_for now skips the NONPROFIT rule when the subtotal equals its minimum (500), so an invoice of exactly EUR 500.00 gets no rebate. The comment claims this keeps an 'inclusive boundary', but the code makes the boundary exclusive.
units.readingNote: Line 13 `if rule.code == "NONPROFIT" and net == rule.minimum_net: continue` contradicts AC3 (exactly EUR 500.00 must get 15%) and its own comment; ask why it was added.

draft.title: Exclude NONPROFIT rebate at exactly the EUR 500 minimum
draft.summary: discount_for now skips the NONPROFIT rule when the subtotal equals its minimum (500), so an invoice of exactly EUR 500.00 gets no rebate. The comment claims this keeps an 'inclusive boundary', but the code makes the boundary exclusive.
draft.readingNote: Line 13 `if rule.code == "NONPROFIT" and net == rule.minimum_net: continue` contradicts AC3 (exactly EUR 500.00 must get 15%) and its own comment; ask why it was added.

facts.why: Existing callers passing discount_code="NONPROFIT" with subtotal exactly 500 previously got 15% via DiscountRule.applies (net >= minimum_net); now they get 0.
Adds a code-specific special-case branch in discount_for's rule loop.

units.title: Test rebate codes, invoice-level code and validation
units.summary: Adds tests for case-insensitive codes, unknown codes, WELCOME on tiny amounts, PARTNER/NONPROFIT just above their minimums, override precedence, taxable/tax/total composition, and rejection of blank codes.
units.readingNote: NONPROFIT is only tested at 500.01 and never at exactly 500.00 or below, so the boundary exclusion in discount_for is not caught; PARTNER below 1000 is not tested either.

draft.title: Test rebate codes, invoice-level code and validation
draft.summary: Adds tests for case-insensitive codes, unknown codes, WELCOME on tiny amounts, PARTNER/NONPROFIT just above their minimums, override precedence, taxable/tax/total composition, and rejection of blank codes.
draft.readingNote: NONPROFIT is only tested at 500.01 and never at exactly 500.00 or below, so the boundary exclusion in discount_for is not caught; PARTNER below 1000 is not tested either.

lines.s: RULES = (DiscountRule("WELCOME", Decimal("0.05")), DiscountRule("PARTNER", Decimal("0.10"), Decimal("1000")), DiscountRule("NONPROFIT", Decimal("0.15"), Decimal("500")))
# Keep the historical inclusive boundary for existing codes.
if rule.code == "NONPROFIT" and net == rule.minimum_net: continue
if not self.number.strip(): raise ValueError("invoice number is required")
if not self.customer.strip(): raise ValueError("customer is required")
if not self.lines: raise ValueError("invoice needs at least one line")
if len(self.currency) != 3 or not self.currency.isalpha(): raise ValueError("currency must be 3 letters")
if self.rebate_code is not None and not self.rebate_code.strip(): raise ValueError("rebate code must not be blank")
def from_lines(cls, number, customer, lines: Iterable[InvoiceLine], currency="EUR"):
def from_lines(cls, number, customer, lines: Iterable[InvoiceLine], currency="EUR", rebate_code=None):
return cls(number, customer, tuple(lines), currency.upper(), rebate_code=rebate_code)
net = money(line.net * (Decimal("1") - discount)); tax = money(net * line.tax.rate)
return LineTotal(line.description, net, tax, money(net + tax))
subtotal = money(sum((line.net for line in invoice.lines), Decimal("0"))); rate = discount_for(discount_code, subtotal)
lines = tuple(calculate_line(line, rate) for line in invoice.lines)
subtotal = money(sum((line.net for line in invoice.lines), Decimal("0")))
# An explicit function argument wins for batch callers; otherwise use the invoice code.
code = discount_code if discount_code is not None else invoice.rebate_code
lines = tuple(calculate_line(line, rebate_rate) for line in invoice.lines)
taxable = money(sum((x.net for x in lines), Decimal("0"))); tax = money(sum((x.tax for x in lines), Decimal("0")))
return InvoiceTotals(subtotal, money(subtotal-taxable), taxable, tax, money(taxable+tax), lines, invoice.currency.upper())
from invoice_engine import Invoice, InvoiceLine, TaxRate, calculate_totals
